macros.Guide_Copy_EN: Follow the Introit: sing, listen, or meditate on the public chant. Keep the posture shown. You do not need to keep pace with the priest’s quiet preparatory prayers.
macros.Concurrency_Rule: Introit is the public liturgical clock while the priest’s preparatory prayers are quiet.

macros.Guide_Copy_EN: Follow the public Kyrie. Keep the posture shown; follow the sung invocations rather than the priest’s private pace.
macros.Concurrency_Rule: Stay with the sung Kyrie until its final invocation.

macros.Guide_Copy_EN: Follow the sung Gloria and the gesture cues attached to its actual words. Change posture only when the active cue tells you to do so.
macros.Next_Reliable_Cue: Collect after the public Gloria ends.
macros.Concurrency_Rule: After the priest’s intonation, the choir carries the public Gloria; return to Priest at the final Amen.

macros.Guide_Copy_EN: Follow the public Collect after Dominus vobiscum and Oremus. Stand and attend to the prayer.
macros.Concurrency_Rule: The Collect is a public priestly prayer.

macros.Guide_Copy_EN: Follow the Epistle / Lesson. Sit and listen to the reading.
macros.Concurrency_Rule: At the end of the Epistle, the interlection chants become the public clock.

macros.Guide_Copy_EN: Follow the Schola: Gradual, then the resolved Alleluia / Tract / Sequence. Remain seated until the Gospel cue approaches.
macros.Concurrency_Rule: When the chant complex ends, the public Gospel becomes the next clock.

macros.Guide_Copy_EN: Follow the public Gospel. Stand; make the three small crosses at the public announcement, then listen attentively.
macros.Next_Reliable_Cue: Sermon if present; otherwise Credo or Offertory.
macros.Concurrency_Rule: The public Gospel controls.

macros.Guide_Copy_EN: Follow the preacher. Sit and listen.
macros.Concurrency_Rule: Follow the preacher; Mass resumes only when the liturgical action resumes.

macros.Guide_Copy_EN: Follow the sung Credo and its public-text gesture cues. Use the active posture cue, especially at the Incarnatus.
macros.Concurrency_Rule: After the priest’s intonation, follow the public sung Creed; return after Amen.

macros.Guide_Copy_EN: While the Offertory chant is sounding, follow the public chant. When it ends, the visible preparation of the altar becomes the main landmark. Remain in the posture shown; respond to incensation only when it actually reaches your section.
macros.Concurrency_Rule: Follow the Offertory chant while sounding; when it ends, the altar action becomes the better landmark.

macros.Guide_Copy_EN: Give priority to the public Orate fratres and response. During the silent Secret, remain recollected rather than trying to synchronize to the priest’s words. Keep the posture shown.
macros.Next_Reliable_Cue: The public Per omnia / Preface dialogue.
macros.Concurrency_Rule: Orate fratres is public; the Secret is quiet but the priest remains the useful clock.

macros.Guide_Copy_EN: Follow the public Preface dialogue and Preface. Stand and answer the dialogue.
macros.Concurrency_Rule: At the end of the Preface, the Sanctus begins.

macros.Guide_Copy_EN: Follow the Schola’s Sanctus / Benedictus while it is actually being sung. Stand through the current chant; prepare to kneel as the Canon takes over.
macros.Concurrency_Rule: Follow Sanctus/Benedictus while sung; when the choir falls silent, the Canon may be followed on the priest track.

macros.Guide_Copy_EN: The main cue is now sacred silence and interior participation. Kneel. Unite yourself with the Sacrifice; remain attentive for the warning bell and visible Consecration landmarks.
macros.Next_Reliable_Cue: Warning bell → Consecration of the Sacred Host.
macros.Concurrency_Rule: The Canon is secret; following the text is optional. Warning bell/elevations override both tracks.

macros.Guide_Copy_EN: The Consecration and visible elevation of the Sacred Host have priority over everything else. Remain kneeling; bow reverently and look upon the Sacred Host when elevated.
macros.Concurrency_Rule: The elevation is the decisive visual/sacramental landmark.

macros.Guide_Copy_EN: The Consecration and visible elevation of the Chalice have priority. Remain kneeling and attend to the elevation.
macros.Concurrency_Rule: The elevation is the decisive visual/sacramental landmark.

macros.Guide_Copy_EN: If the Benedictus resumes, follow that public chant; otherwise the main mode is sacred silence and interior participation. Keep the posture of your local/profile setting.
macros.Concurrency_Rule: If Benedictus resumes, follow it; otherwise remain in sacred silence / priest Canon.

macros.Guide_Copy_EN: Follow the visible minor elevation and then the public Per omnia. Use the public conclusion as the clean reset into the Communion rite.
macros.Concurrency_Rule: Minor elevation and public Per omnia reset the common timeline.

macros.Guide_Copy_EN: Follow the public Pater noster and the Sed libera response. Stand and make the response when it is actually due.
macros.Concurrency_Rule: Pater noster is public.

macros.Guide_Copy_EN: During silent Libera nos, use the visible Fraction as the landmark; when Pax Domini is heard, the public cue takes priority. Stand until the next posture cue.
macros.Concurrency_Rule: After Pax Domini the Agnus becomes the public sung clock.

macros.Guide_Copy_EN: Follow the sung Agnus Dei. Make the ordinary breast strikes with the sung invocations; prepare to kneel for Communion preparation.
macros.Concurrency_Rule: After Agnus, private Communion preparation follows.

macros.Guide_Copy_EN: The main mode is recollection and interior preparation for Communion. Kneel and prepare yourself for Communion.
macros.Concurrency_Rule: Priest’s private prayers may be followed, but interior preparation is primary.

macros.Guide_Copy_EN: The visible Communion of the priest is now the main landmark. Remain kneeling and prepare for the public Communion invitation if the faithful will receive.
macros.Next_Reliable_Cue: Ecce Agnus Dei, if the faithful receive.
macros.Concurrency_Rule: Visible Communion of the priest is the landmark.

macros.Guide_Copy_EN: The public Ecce Agnus Dei and the faithful’s Domine non sum dignus have priority. Remain kneeling and make the response/associated action when it is actually due.
macros.Concurrency_Rule: Once distribution begins, the Communion chant is useful while waiting.

macros.Guide_Copy_EN: Your personal Communion action has priority when your turn actually comes; otherwise follow the Communion chant and visible distribution. Approach, receive, and return according to your actual place in the Communion line.
macros.Concurrency_Rule: Your own Communion turn overrides both tracks; otherwise follow Communion chant/distribution.

macros.Guide_Copy_EN: If the Communion chant is still sounding, follow it; otherwise the priest’s visible return and ablutions are the main landmark. Use the local/profile posture shown and prepare to stand for the Postcommunion.
macros.Concurrency_Rule: Stay with Communion chant while it sounds; switch when chant/distribution end and ablutions dominate.

macros.Guide_Copy_EN: Follow the public Postcommunion after Dominus vobiscum and Oremus. Stand and attend to the prayer.
macros.Concurrency_Rule: Postcommunion is public.

macros.Guide_Copy_EN: Follow the public dismissal and response. Stand and make the response.
macros.Concurrency_Rule: Dismissal is public; Schola/people give the response.

macros.Guide_Copy_EN: During the quiet Placeat, remain recollected. When the priest turns for the final blessing, that public visible action takes priority. Kneel for the blessing where appointed, then rise for the Last Gospel.
macros.Concurrency_Rule: Quiet Placeat leads into the visible final blessing.

macros.Guide_Copy_EN: Follow the public Last Gospel. Stand; genuflect at Et Verbum caro factum est, then rise.
macros.Concurrency_Rule: Last Gospel is the public final text unless omitted by a special branch.

blocks.Section: Prayers at the Foot of the Altar
blocks.Title: Judica me, Deus (Psalm 42)
blocks.Latin_Text:
S. Iúdica me, Deus, et discérne causam meam de gente non sancta: ab hómine iníquo et dolóso érue me.
M. Quia tu es, Deus, fortitudo mea: quare me reppulísti, et quare tristis incédo, dum afflígit me inimícus?
S. Emítte lucem tuam et veritátem tuam: ipsa me deduxérunt, et adduxérunt in montem sanctum tuum et in tabernácula tua.
M. Et introíbo ad altáre Dei: ad Deum, qui lætíficat iuventútem meam.
S. Confitébor tibi in cíthara, Deus, Deus meus: quare tristis es, ánima mea, et quare contúrbas me?
M. Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.
S. Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
M. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper: et in saecula sæculórum. Amen.
℣. Introíbo ad altáre Dei.
℟. Ad Deum, qui lætíficat iuventútem meam.
blocks.English_Text:
Judge me, O God, and distinguish my cause from the nation that is not holy: deliver me from the unjust and deceitful man.
For Thou, O God, art my strength: why hast Thou cast me off? and why do I go sorrowful whilst the enemy afflicteth me?
Send forth Thy light and Thy truth: they have led me and brought me unto Thy holy hill, and into Thy tabernacles.
And I will go in unto the Altar of God: unto God, Who giveth joy to my youth.
I will praise Thee upon the harp, O God, my God: why art thou sad, O my soul? and why dost thou disquiet me?
Hope thou in God, for I will yet praise Him: Who is the salvation of my countenance, and my God.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

℟. Unto God, Who giveth joy to my youth.

blocks.Section: Prayers at the Foot of the Altar
blocks.Title: Confiteor — Celebrant
blocks.Latin_Text: Confíteor Deo omnipoténti, beátæ Maríæ semper Vírgini, beáto Michaéli Archángelo, beáto Ioánni Baptístæ, sanctis Apóstolis Petro et Paulo, ómnibus Sanctis, et vobis, fratres: quia peccávi nimis cogitatióne, verbo et opere: mea culpa, mea culpa, mea máxima culpa. Ideo precor beátam Maríam semper Vírginem, beátum Michaélem Archángelum, beátum Ioánnem Baptístam, sanctos Apóstolos Petrum et Paulum, omnes Sanctos, et vos, fratres, oráre pro me ad Dóminum Deum nostrum.
blocks.English_Text: I confess to almighty God, to blessed Mary ever Virgin, to blessed Michael the Archangel, to blessed John the Baptist, to the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, to all the Saints, and to you, brethren, that I have sinned exceedingly in thought, word and deed: through my fault, through my fault, through my most grievous fault. Therefore I beseech blessed Mary ever Virgin, blessed Michael the Archangel, blessed John the Baptist, the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, all the Saints, and you, brethren, to pray to the Lord our God for me.

Salus pópuli ego sum, dicit Dóminus: de quacúmque tribulatióne clamáverint ad me, exáudiam eos: et ero illórum Dóminus in perpétuum.

blocks.Latin_Text:
Léctio Epístolæ beáti Pauli Apóstoli ad Ephésios.
Fratres: Renovámini spíritu mentis vestræ, et indúite novum hóminem, qui secúndum Deum creátus est in iustítia et sanctitáte veritátis. Propter quod deponéntes mendácium, loquímini veritátem unusquísque cum próximo suo: quóniam sumus ínvicem membra. Irascímini, et nolíte peccáre: sol non occídat super iracúndiam vestram. Nolíte locum dare diábolo: qui furabátur, iam non furétur; magis autem labóret, operándo mánibus suis, quod bonum est, ut hábeat, unde tríbuat necessitátem patiénti.
℟. Deo grátias.
blocks.English_Text:
Lesson from the Epistle of blessed Paul the Apostle to the Ephesians.
Brethren: Be renewed in the spirit of your mind, and put on the new man, who according to God is created in justice and holiness of truth. Therefore, putting away falsehood, let each speak truth with his neighbour, for we are members one of another. Be angry, and sin not; let not the sun go down upon your anger. Give no place to the devil. He that stole, let him now steal no more, but rather let him labour, working with his hands at that which is good, that he may have wherewith to give to him that suffereth need.
℟. Thanks be to God.

blocks.Title: Holy Gospel — Matthew 22:1–14
blocks.Latin_Text:
In illo témpore: Loquebátur Iesus princípibus sacerdótum et pharisǽis in parábolis, dicens: Símile factum est regnum cœlórum hómini regi, qui fecit núptias fílio suo. Et misit servos suos vocáre invitátos ad núptias, et nolébant veníre. Iterum misit álios servos, dicens: Dícite invitátis: Ecce, prándium meum parávi, tauri mei et altília occísa sunt, et ómnia paráta: veníte ad núptias. Illi autem neglexérunt: et abiérunt, álius in villam suam, álius vero ad negotiatiónem suam: réliqui vero tenuérunt servos eius, et contuméliis afféctos occidérunt. Rex autem cum audísset, irátus est: et, missis exercítibus suis, pérdidit homicídas illos et civitátem illórum succéndit. Tunc ait servis suis: Núptiæ quidem parátæ sunt, sed, qui invitáti erant, non fuérunt digni. Ite ergo ad éxitus viárum et, quoscúmque invenéritis, vocáte ad núptias. Et egréssi servi eius in vias, congregavérunt omnes, quos invenérunt, malos et bonos: et implétæ sunt núptiæ discumbéntium. Intrávit autem rex, ut vidéret discumbéntes, et vidit ibi hóminem non vestítum veste nuptiáli. Et ait illi: Amíce, quómodo huc intrásti non habens vestem nuptiálem? At ille obmútuit. Tunc dixit rex minístris: Ligátis mánibus et pédibus eius, míttite eum in ténebras exterióres: ibi erit fletus et stridor déntium. Multi enim sunt vocáti, pauci vero elécti.
℟. Laus tibi, Christe.
Per evangélica dicta deleántur nostra delícta.
blocks.English_Text:
At that time Jesus spoke to the chief priests and Pharisees in parables, saying: The kingdom of heaven is like a king who made a marriage feast for his son. He sent his servants to call those invited to the wedding, but they would not come. Again he sent other servants, saying: Tell those who are invited: Behold, I have prepared my banquet; my oxen and fattened cattle are killed, and all things are ready; come to the wedding. But they paid no heed and went away, one to his farm and another to his business; the rest seized his servants, treated them shamefully, and killed them. When the king heard of it he was angry, and sent his armies, destroyed those murderers, and burned their city. Then he said to his servants: The wedding indeed is ready, but those who were invited were not worthy. Go therefore to the crossroads, and whomever you shall find, call to the wedding. Going out into the roads, the servants gathered all whom they found, bad and good alike, and the wedding was filled with guests. The king entered to see the guests and saw there a man not clothed in a wedding garment. He said to him: Friend, how didst thou enter here without a wedding garment? But he was speechless. Then the king said to the servants: Bind his hands and feet and cast him into the outer darkness; there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth. For many are called, but few are chosen.
℟. Praise be to Thee, O Christ.
By the words of the Gospel may our sins be blotted out.

blocks.Title: Credo in unum Deum
blocks.Latin_Text: Credo in unum Deum. Patrem omnipoténtem, factórem cæli et terræ, visibílium ómnium et invisibílium. Et in unum Dóminum Iesum Christum, Fílium Dei unigénitum. Et ex Patre natum ante ómnia sæcula. Deum de Deo, lumen de lúmine, Deum verum de Deo vero. Génitum, non factum, consubstantiálem Patri: per quem ómnia facta sunt. Qui propter nos hómines et propter nostram salútem descéndit de cælis. Et incarnátus est de Spíritu Sancto ex María Vírgine: et homo factus est. Crucifíxus étiam pro nobis: sub Póntio Piláto passus, et sepúltus est. Et resurréxit tértia die, secúndum Scriptúras. Et ascéndit in cælum: sedet ad déxteram Patris. Et íterum ventúrus est cum glória iudicáre vivos et mórtuos: cuius regni non erit finis. Et in Spíritum Sanctum, Dóminum et vivificántem: qui ex Patre Filióque procédit. Qui cum Patre et Fílio simul adorátur et conglorificátur: qui locútus est per Prophétas. Et unam sanctam cathólicam et apostólicam Ecclésiam. Confíteor unum baptísma in remissiónem peccatórum. Et exspécto resurrectiónem mortuórum. Et vitam ✠ ventúri sæculi. Amen.
blocks.English_Text: I believe in one God. The Father almighty, maker of heaven and earth, and of all things visible and invisible. And in one Lord Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son of God; born of the Father before all ages. God of God, light of light, true God of true God. Begotten, not made, consubstantial with the Father: by whom all things were made. Who for us men, and for our salvation, came down from heaven. And was incarnate by the Holy Ghost of the Virgin Mary: and was made man. He was crucified also for us, suffered under Pontius Pilate, and was buried. And on the third day He rose again according to the Scriptures. And He ascended into heaven, and sitteth at the right hand of the Father. And He shall come again with glory to judge the living and the dead: of Whose kingdom there shall be no end. And in the Holy Ghost, the Lord and Giver of Life: Who proceedeth from the Father and the Son. Who together with the Father and the Son is together adored and glorified: who spoke by the Prophets. And in One, Holy, Catholic and Apostolic Church. I confess one Baptism for the remission of sins. And I look for the resurrection of the dead. And the life of the world to come. Amen.

blocks.Title: Suscipe, sancte Pater
blocks.Latin_Text: Suscipe, sancte Pater, omnipotens ætérne Deus, hanc immaculátam hóstiam, quam ego indígnus fámulus tuus óffero tibi Deo meo vivo et vero, pro innumerabílibus peccátis, et offensiónibus, et neglegéntiis meis, et pro ómnibus circumstántibus, sed et pro ómnibus fidélibus christiánis vivis atque defúnctis: ut mihi, et illis profíciat ad salútem in vitam ætérnam. blocks.English_Text: Accept, O Holy father, Almighty and Eternal God, this spotless host, which I, Your unworthy servant, offer to You, my living and true God, to atone for my numberless sins, offences, and negligences; on behalf of all here present and likewise for all faithful Christians living and dead, that it may profit me and them as a means of salvation to life everlasting. Amen.

blocks.Title: Deus, qui humanae substantiae
blocks.Latin_Text: Deus, qui humánæ substántiæ dignitátem mirabíliter condidísti, et mirabílius reformásti: da nobis per huius aquæ et vini mystérium, eius divinitátis esse consórtes, qui humanitátis nostræ fíeri dignátus est párticeps, Iesus Christus, Fílius tuus, Dóminus noster: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti Deus: per ómnia saecula sæculórum. Amen.
blocks.English_Text: O God, who wonderfully created the dignity of human nature and still more wonderfully restored it: grant us by the mystery of this water and wine to be made partakers of his divinity, who vouchsafed to become partaker of our humanity, Jesus Christ thy Son our Lord: who liveth and reigneth with thee in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end. Amen.

blocks.Title: Offerimus tibi, Domine
blocks.Latin_Text: Offérimus tibi, Dómine, cálicem salutáris, tuam deprecántes cleméntiam: ut in conspéctu divínæ maiestátis tuæ, pro nostra et totíus mundi salute, cum odóre suavitátis ascéndat. Amen.

blocks.Title: Lavabo inter innocentes (Psalm 25)
blocks.Latin_Text:
Ps 25, 6–12
Lavábo inter innocéntes manus meas: et circúmdabo altáre tuum, Dómine:
Ut áudiam vocem laudis, et enárrem univérsa mirabília tua.
Dómine, diléxi decórem domus tuæ et locum habitatiónis glóriæ tuæ.
Ne perdas cum ímpiis, Deus, ánimam meam, et cum viris sánguinum vitam meam:
In quorum mánibus iniquitátes sunt: déxtera eórum repléta est munéribus.
Ego autem in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum: rédime me et miserére mei.
Pes meus stetit in dirécto: in ecclésiis benedícam te, Dómine. Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper: et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
blocks.English_Text:
Ps 25, 6–12
I will wash my hands among the innocent, and I will encompass Thine Altar, O Lord.

In whose hands are iniquities, their right hand is filled with gifts.
But as for me, I have walked in my innocence; redeem me, and have mercy on me.

blocks.Title: Suscipe, sancta Trinitas
blocks.Latin_Text: Súscipe, sancta Trinitas, hanc oblatiónem, quam tibi offérimus ob memóriam passiónis, resurrectiónis, et ascensiónis Iesu Christi, Dómini nostri: et in honórem beátæ Maríæ semper Vírginis, et beáti Ioannis Baptistæ, et sanctórum Apostolórum Petri et Pauli, et istórum et ómnium Sanctórum: ut illis profíciat ad honórem, nobis autem ad salútem: et illi pro nobis intercédere dignéntur in coelis, quorum memóriam ágimus in terris. Per eúndem Christum, Dóminum nostrum. Amen.
blocks.English_Text: Receive, O Holy Trinity, this oblation which we make to Thee in memory of the Passion, Resurrection and Ascension of our Lord Jesus Christ; and in honor of Blessed Mary ever Virgin, of blessed John the Baptist, the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, of these and of all the Saints. To them let it bring honor, and to us salvation, and may they whom we are commemorating here on earth deign to plead for us in heaven. Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

blocks.Title: Preface of the Most Holy Trinity
blocks.Latin_Text: Vere dignum et iustum est, æquum et salutáre, nos tibi semper et ubíque grátias ágere: Dómine sancte, Pater omnípotens, ætérne Deus: Qui cum unigénito Fílio tuo et Spíritu Sancto unus es Deus, unus es Dóminus: non in uníus singularitáte persónæ, sed in uníus Trinitáte substántiæ. Quod enim de tua glória, revelánte te, crédimus, hoc de Fílio tuo, hoc de Spíritu Sancto sine differéntia discretiónis sentímus. Ut in confessióne veræ sempiternǽque Deitátis, et in persónis propríetas, et in esséntia únitas, et in maiestáte adorétur æquálitas. Quam laudant Angeli atque Archángeli, Chérubim quoque ac Séraphim: qui non cessant clamáre cotídie, una voce dicéntes:
blocks.English_Text: It is truly meet and just, right and profitable unto salvation, that we should at all times and in all places give thanks unto Thee, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: Who with Thine only-begotten Son and the Holy Ghost art one God, one Lord; not in the singleness of one Person, but in the Trinity of one substance. For what, by Thy revelation, we believe of Thy glory, the same we believe of Thy Son and of the Holy Ghost, without difference or distinction; so that, in confessing the true and everlasting Godhead, distinction in Persons, unity in essence, and equality in majesty may be adored. Which the Angels and Archangels, the Cherubim also and Seraphim praise, who cease not daily to cry out with one voice, saying:

blocks.Latin_Text: Te igitur, clementíssime Pater, per Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum, Dóminum nostrum, súpplices rogámus, ac pétimus, uti accepta habeas et benedícas, hæc ✠ dona, hæc ✠ múnera, hæc ✠ sancta sacrifícia illibáta. In primis, quæ tibi offérimus pro Ecclésia tua sancta cathólica: quam pacificáre, custodíre, adunáre et régere dignéris toto orbe terrárum: una cum fámulo tuo Papa nostro N. et Antístite nostro et ómnibus orthodóxis, atque cathólicæ et apostólicae fídei cultóribus.
blocks.English_Text: Therefore, most merciful Father, through Jesus Christ thy Son our Lord, we humbly pray and beseech thee, that thou wouldst accept and bless, these gifts, these offerings, these holy and unspotted sacrifices. We offer them up to Thee, in the first place, for Thy Holy Catholic Church, that it may please Thee to grant her peace, to preserve, unite, and govern her throughout the world; as also for Thy servant N. our Pope, and N. our Bishop, and for all orthodox believers and all who profess the Catholic and Apostolic faith.

blocks.Title: Memento, Domine — Living
blocks.Latin_Text: Meménto, Dómine, famulórum famularúmque tuarum N. et N. et ómnium circumstántium, quorum tibi fides cógnita est et nota devótio, pro quibus tibi offérimus: vel qui tibi ófferunt hoc sacrifícium laudis, pro se suísque ómnibus: pro redemptióne animárum suárum, pro spe salútis et incolumitátis suæ: tibíque reddunt vota sua ætérno Deo, vivo et vero.
blocks.English_Text: Remember, O Lord, thy servants and handmaids N. and N. and of all here present, whose faith and devotion are known to Thee, for whom we offer, or who offer up to Thee this Sacrifice of praise for themselves and all those dear to them, for the redemption of their souls and the hope of their safety and salvation: who now pay their vows to Thee, the everlasting, living and true God.

blocks.Title: Communicantes
blocks.Latin_Text: Communicántes, et memóriam venerántes, in primis gloriósæ semper Vírginis Maríæ, Genetrícis Dei et Dómini nostri Iesu Christi: sed et beati Ioseph, eiusdem Virginis Sponsi, et beatórum Apostolórum ac Mártyrum tuórum, Petri et Pauli, Andréæ, Iacóbi, Ioánnis, Thomæ, Iacóbi, Philíppi, Bartholomaei, Matthaei, Simónis et Thaddaei: Lini, Cleti, Cleméntis, Xysti, Cornélii, Cypriáni, Lauréntii, Chrysógoni, Ioánnis et Pauli, Cosmæ et Damiáni: et ómnium Sanctórum tuórum; quorum méritis precibúsque concédas, ut in ómnibus protectiónis tuæ muniámur auxílio. Per eúndem Christum, Dóminum nostrum. Amen.
blocks.English_Text: In communion with, and venerating the memory first of the glorious ever-Virgin Mary, Mother of our God and Lord Jesus Christ: also of blessed Joseph, her Spouse; and likewise of Thy blessed Apostles and Martyrs, Peter and Paul, Andrew, James, John, Thomas, James, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Simon and Thaddeus, Linus, Cletus, Clement, Sixtus, Cornelius, Cyprian, Lawrence, Chrysogonus, John and Paul, Cosmas and Damian, and of all Thy Saints. Grant for the sake of their merits and prayers that in all things we may be guarded and helped by Thy protection. Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

blocks.Title: Hanc igitur
blocks.Latin_Text: Hanc igitur oblatiónem servitutis nostræ, sed et cunctae famíliæ tuæ, quaesumus, Dómine, ut placátus accípias: diésque nostros in tua pace dispónas, atque ab ætérna damnatióne nos éripi, et in electórum tuórum iúbeas grege numerári. Per Christum, Dóminum nostrum. Amen.
blocks.English_Text: O Lord, we beseech Thee, graciously to accept this oblation of our service and that of Thy whole household. Order our days in Thy peace, and command that we be rescued from eternal damnation and numbered in the flock of Thine elect. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

blocks.Title: Quam oblationem
blocks.Latin_Text: Quam oblatiónem tu, Deus, in ómnibus, quaesumus, bene ✠ díctam, adscríp ✠ tam, ra ✠ tam, rationábilem, acceptabilémque fácere dignéris: ut nobis Cor ✠ pus, et San ✠ guis fiat dilectíssimi Fílii tui, Dómini nostri Iesu Christi.
blocks.English_Text: Which offering do thou, O God, we beseech thee, make blessed, approved, ratified, reasonable and acceptable: that it may become for us the Body, and Blood of thy most beloved Son, our Lord Jesus Christ.

blocks.Title: Qui pridie · Consecration of the Host
blocks.Latin_Text: Qui prídie quam paterétur, accépit panem in sanctas ac venerábiles manus suas, elevátis óculis in coelum ad te Deum, Patrem suum omnipoténtem, tibi grátias agens, bene ✠ dixit, fregit, dedítque discípulis suis, dicens: Accípite, et manducáte ex hoc omnes. HOC EST ENIM CORPUS MEUM.
blocks.English_Text: Who, the day before he suffered, took bread into his holy and venerable hands, and with eyes lifted up to heaven unto thee, God, his almighty Father, giving thanks to thee, he blessed it, broke it, and gave it to his disciples, saying: Take and eat ye all of this. FOR THIS IS MY BODY.

blocks.Title: Simili modo · Consecration of the Chalice
blocks.Latin_Text: Símili modo postquam coenátum est, accípiens et hunc præclárum Cálicem in sanctas ac venerábiles manus suas: item tibi grátias agens, bene ✠ dixit, dedítque discípulis suis, dicens: Accípite, et bíbite ex eo omnes. HIC EST ENIM CALIX SÁNGUINIS MEI, NOVI ET ÆTÉRNI TESTAMÉNTI: MYSTÉRIUM FÍDEI: QUI PRO VOBIS ET PRO MULTIS EFFUNDÉTUR IN REMISSIÓNEM PECCATÓRUM. Hæc quotiescúmque fecéritis, in mei memóriam faciétis.
blocks.English_Text: In like manner, after he had supped, taking also this excellent Chalice into his holy and venerable hands: again giving thanks to thee, he blessed it, and gave it to his disciples, saying: Take and drink ye all of this. FOR THIS IS THE CHALICE OF MY BLOOD, OF THE NEW AND ETERNAL TESTAMENT: THE MYSTERY OF FAITH: WHICH SHALL BE SHED FOR YOU AND FOR MANY UNTO THE REMISSION OF SINS. blocks.Title: Unde et memores
blocks.Latin_Text: Unde et mémores, Dómine, nos servi tui, sed et plebs tua sancta, eiusdem Christi Fílii tui, Dómini nostri, tam beátæ passiónis, nec non et ab ínferis resurrectiónis, sed et in coelos gloriósæ ascensiónis: offérimus præcláræ maiestáti tuæ de tuis donis ac datis, hóstiam ✠ puram, hóstiam ✠ sanctam, hóstiam ✠ immaculátam, Panem ✠ sanctum vitæ ætérnæ, et Calicem ✠ salútis perpétuæ.
blocks.English_Text: Wherefore, O Lord, we Thy servants, and Thy holy people also, calling to mind the blessed Passion of the same Christ Thy Son our Lord, as also His Resurrection from the grave and glorious Ascension into heaven: offer unto thy excellent majesty of thy gifts and grants, a pure victim, a holy victim, an immaculate victim, the holy Bread of eternal life and the Chalice of everlasting salvation.

blocks.Title: Supra quae
blocks.Latin_Text: Supra quæ propítio ac seréno vultu respícere dignéris: et accépta habére, sicúti accépta habére dignátus es múnera púeri tui iusti Abel, et sacrifícium Patriárchæ nostri Abrahæ: et quod tibi óbtulit summus sacérdos tuus Melchísedech, sanctum sacrifícium, immaculátam hóstiam.
blocks.English_Text: Deign to look upon them with a favorable and gracious countenance, and to accept them as Thou didst accept the offerings of Thy just servant Abel, and the sacrifice of our Patriarch Abraham, and that which Thy high priest Melchisedech offered up to Thee, a holy Sacrifice, an immaculate Victim.

blocks.Title: Supplices te rogamus
blocks.Latin_Text: Súpplices te rogámus, omnípotens Deus: iube hæc perférri per manus sancti Angeli tui in sublíme altáre tuum, in conspéctu divínæ maiestátis tuæ: ut, quotquot ex hac altáris participatióne sacrosánctum Fílii tui Cor ✠ pus, et Sán ✠ guinem sumpsérimus, omni benedictióne coelésti et grátia repleámur. Per eúndem Christum, Dóminum nostrum. Amen.
blocks.English_Text: Humbly we beseech Thee, almighty God, to command that these our offerings be carried by the hands of Thy holy Angel to Thine Altar on high, in the sight of Thy divine Majesty: that as many of us as shall receive from this altar the most sacred Body and Blood of thy Son, may be filled with every heavenly blessing and grace. Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

blocks.Title: Memento etiam, Domine — Dead
blocks.Latin_Text: Meménto étiam, Dómine, famulórum famularúmque tuárum N. et N., qui nos præcessérunt cum signo fídei, et dórmiunt in somno pacis. Ipsis, Dómine, et ómnibus in Christo quiescéntibus locum refrigérii, lucis pacis ut indúlgeas, deprecámur. Per eúndem Christum, Dóminum nostrum. Amen.
blocks.English_Text: Remember also, O Lord, thy servants and handmaids N. and N. who have gone before us with the sign of faith and sleep the sleep of peace. To these, O Lord, and to all who rest in Christ, grant, we beseech thee, a place of refreshment, light and peace. Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

blocks.Title: Nobis quoque peccatoribus
blocks.Latin_Text: Nobis quoque peccatóribus fámulis tuis, de multitúdine miseratiónum tuárum sperántibus, partem áliquam et societátem donáre dignéris, cum tuis sanctis Apóstolis et Martýribus: cum Ioánne, Stéphano, Matthía, Bárnaba, Ignátio, Alexándro, Marcellíno, Petro, Felicitáte, Perpétua, Agatha, Lúcia, Agnéte, Cæcília, Anastásia, et ómnibus Sanctis tuis: intra quorum nos consórtium, non æstimátor mériti, sed véniæ, quaesumus, largítor admítte. Per Christum, Dóminum nostrum.
blocks.English_Text: To us also, thy sinful servants who put our trust in the multitude of Thy mercies, vouchsafe to grant some part and fellowship with Thy holy Apostles and Martyrs: with John, Stephen, Matthias, Barnabas, Ignatius, Alexander, Marcellinus, Peter, Felicitas, Perpetua, Agatha, Lucy, Agnes, Cecilia, Anastasia, and all Thy Saints. Into their company we beseech Thee admit us, not considering our merits, but freely pardoning our offenses. Through Christ our Lord.

blocks.Title: Pater noster
blocks.Latin_Text:
Pater noster, qui es in cælis: sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris: et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem.
℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.

blocks.Title: Domine Iesu Christe, Fili Dei vivi
blocks.Latin_Text: Dómine Iesu Christe, Fili Dei vivi, qui ex voluntáte Patris, cooperánte Spíritu Sancto, per mortem tuam mundum vivificásti: líbera me per hoc sacrosánctum Corpus et Sánguinem tuum ab ómnibus iniquitátibus meis, et univérsis malis: et fac me tuis semper inhærére mandátis, et a te numquam separári permíttas: Qui cum eódem Deo Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas Deus in saecula sæculórum. Amen.
blocks.English_Text: O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, Who, by the will of the Father and the co-operation of the Holy Ghost, hast by Thy death given life to the world: deliver me by this, Thy most sacred Body and Blood, from all my iniquities and from every evil; make me cling always to Thy commandments, and permit me never to be separated from Thee. Who with the same God, the Father and the Holy Ghost, livest and reignest God, world without end. Amen.

blocks.Title: Perceptio Corporis tui
blocks.Latin_Text: Percéptio Córporis tui, Dómine Iesu Christe, quod ego indígnus súmere præsúmo, non mihi provéniat in iudícium et condemnatiónem: sed pro tua pietáte prosit mihi ad tutaméntum mentis et córporis, et ad medélam percipiéndam: Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre in unitáte Spíritus Sancti Deus, per ómnia saecula sæculórum. Amen.
blocks.English_Text: Let not the partaking of Thy Body, O Lord Jesus Christ, which I, though unworthy, presume to receive, turn to my judgment and condemnation; but through Thy mercy may it be unto me a safeguard and a healing remedy both of soul and body. Who livest and reignest with God the Father, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end. Amen.

blocks.Title: Placeat tibi, sancta Trinitas
blocks.Latin_Text:
Pláceat tibi, sancta Trínitas, obséquium servitútis meæ: et præsta; ut sacrifícium,
quod óculis tuæ maiestátis indígnus óbtuli, tibi sit acceptábile, mihíque et ómnibus,
pro quibus illud óbtuli, sit, te miseránte, propitiábile. Per Christum Dóminum nostrum. Amen.
blocks.English_Text:
May the homage of my service be pleasing to Thee, O holy Trinity; and grant that the sacrifice which I,
though unworthy, have offered in the sight of Thy Majesty, may be acceptable to Thee, and through Thy mercy
be a propitiation for me and for all those for whom I have offered it. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

blocks.Title: In principio erat Verbum · Last Gospel
blocks.Latin_Text:
In princípio erat Verbum, et Verbum erat apud Deum, et Deus erat Verbum. Hoc erat in princípio apud Deum.
Ómnia per ipsum facta sunt: et sine ipso factum est nihil, quod factum est. In ipso vita erat, et vita erat lux hóminum:
et lux in ténebris lucet, et ténebræ eam non comprehendérunt.
Fuit homo missus a Deo, cui nomen erat Ioánnes. Hic venit in testimónium, ut testimónium perhibéret de lúmine,
ut omnes créderent per illum. Non erat ille lux, sed ut testimónium perhibéret de lúmine. Erat lux vera,
quæ illúminat omnem hóminem veniéntem in hunc mundum. In mundo erat, et mundus per ipsum factus est,
et mundus eum non cognóvit. In própria venit, et sui eum non recepérunt. Quotquot autem recepérunt eum,
dedit eis potestátem fílios Dei fíeri, his, qui credunt in nómine eius: qui non ex sanguínibus, neque ex voluntáte carnis,
neque ex voluntáte viri, sed ex Deo nati sunt.
ET VERBUM CARO FACTUM EST.
Et habitávit in nobis: et vídimus glóriam eius, glóriam quasi Unigéniti a Patre, plenum grátiæ et veritátis.
℟. Deo grátias.
blocks.English_Text:
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God.
All things were made by Him; and without Him was made nothing that was made. In Him was life, and the life was the light of men.
And the light shineth in darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it.
There was a man sent from God, whose name was John. This man came for a witness, to give testimony of the light,
that all men might believe through him. He was not the light, but was to give testimony of the light. That was the true light,
which enlighteneth every man that cometh into this world. He was in the world, and the world was made by Him, and the world knew Him not.
He came unto His own, and His own received Him not. But as many as received Him, He gave them power to be made the sons of God,
to them that believe in His name: who are born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.
AND THE WORD WAS MADE FLESH.
And dwelt among us; and we saw his glory, the glory as of the Only-begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth.
Thanks be to God.

priestEvents.Trigger_Text: Fílium Dei unigénitum. Et ex Patre natum ante ómnia sæcula. Deum de Deo, lumen de lúmine, Deum verum de Deo vero. Génitum, non factum, consubstantiálem Patri: per quem ómnia facta sunt.
priestEvents.Posture: Standing for intonation/recitation; may sit while schola continues
priestEvents.Action: Raises head; continues recitation.

priestEvents.Trigger_Text: Qui propter nos hómines et propter nostram salútem descéndit de cælis.
priestEvents.Posture: Standing for intonation/recitation; may sit while schola continues
priestEvents.Action: Continues recitation.

priestEvents.Trigger_Text: Et incarnátus est de Spíritu Sancto ex María Vírgine: et homo factus est.

priestEvents.Trigger_Text: Crucifíxus étiam pro nobis: sub Póntio Piláto passus, et sepúltus est. Et resurréxit tértia die, secúndum Scriptúras. Et ascéndit in cælum: sedet ad déxteram Patris.

priestEvents.Trigger_Text: Et íterum ventúrus est cum glória iudicáre vivos et mórtuos: cuius regni non erit finis.

priestEvents.Action: Continues recitation.

priestEvents.Trigger_Text: Et in Spíritum Sanctum, Dóminum et vivificántem: qui ex Patre Filióque procédit.

priestEvents.Trigger_Text: Et unam sanctam cathólicam et apostólicam Ecclésiam. Confíteor unum baptísma in remissiónem peccatórum. Et exspécto resurrectiónem mortuórum.

priestEvents.Action: Continues recitation.

priestEvents.Trigger_Text: Suscipe, sancte Pater, omnipotens ætérne Deus, hanc immaculátam hóstiam, quam ego indígnus fámulus tuus óffero tibi Deo meo vivo et vero, pro innumerabílibus peccátis, et offensiónibus, et neglegéntiis meis, et pro ómnibus circumstántibus, sed et pro ómnibus fidélibus christiánis vivis atque defúnctis: ut mihi, et illis profíciat ad salútem in vitam ætérnam. Amen.
priestEvents.Action: Holds the Paten with the Host elevated at chest level; raises eyes to God then immediately lowers them and offers the Host while praying.

priestEvents.Trigger_Text: [MAKES THE CROSS WITH THE PATEN — PLACES THE HOST — SETS THE PATEN ASIDE]

priestEvents.Trigger_Text: Deus, qui humánæ substántiæ dignitátem mirabíliter condidísti, et mirabílius reformásti:

priestEvents.Trigger_Text: da nobis per huius aquæ et vini mystérium, eius divinitátis esse consórtes, qui humanitátis nostræ fíeri dignátus est párticeps, Iesus Christus, Fílius tuus, Dóminus noster: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti Deus: per ómnia saecula sæculórum. Amen.
priestEvents.Action: Pours a little water into the Chalice while continuing the prayer.

priestEvents.Trigger_Text: Offérimus tibi, Dómine, cálicem salutáris, tuam deprecántes cleméntiam: ut in conspéctu divínæ maiestátis tuæ, pro nostra et totíus mundi salute, cum odóre suavitátis ascéndat. Amen.
priestEvents.Action: At the centre, holds the uncovered Chalice elevated with both hands and eyes directed toward God while offering it.

priestEvents.Trigger_Text: [MAKES THE CROSS WITH THE CHALICE — PLACES AND COVERS IT]
priestEvents.Action: After the prayer, makes the Sign of the Cross with the Chalice over the corporal, places it behind the Host, and covers it with the Pall.

priestEvents.Trigger_Text: In spíritu humilitátis et in ánimo contríto suscipiámur a te, Dómine: et sic fiat sacrifícium nostrum in conspéctu tuo hódie, ut pláceat tibi, Dómine Deus.
priestEvents.Action: Bows profoundly with hands joined on altar

priestEvents.Trigger_Text: [STANDS ERECT — RAISES EYES AND HANDS — JOINS HANDS]
priestEvents.Action: Stands erect, raises eyes and hands, then joins the hands before the breast in preparation for the blessing.

priestEvents.Trigger_Text: Veni, sanctificátor omnípotens ætérne Deus:
priestEvents.Action: Says the opening with hands joined.

priestEvents.Trigger_Text: et bene ✠ dic hoc sacrifícium, tuo sancto nómini præparátum.
priestEvents.Action: Makes the Sign of the Cross over Host and Chalice at benedic.

priestEvents.Trigger_Text: Per intercessiónem beáti Michaélis Archángeli, stantis a dextris altáris incénsi, et ómnium electórum suórum, incénsum istud dignétur Dóminus bene ✠ dícere, et in odórem suavitátis accípere. Per Christum, Dóminum nostrum. Amen.
priestEvents.Action: Blesses incense with Sign of Cross.

priestEvents.Trigger_Text: Incénsum istud a te benedíctum ascéndat ad te, Dómine: et descéndat super nos misericórdia tua.
priestEvents.Action: Incenses the oblations with prescribed swings.

priestEvents.Trigger_Text:
Ps 140, 2–4
Dirigátur, Dómine, orátio mea, sicut incénsum, in conspéctu tuo: elevátio mánuum meárum sacrifícium vespertínum.
Pone, Dómine, custódiam ori meo, et óstium circumstántiæ lábiis meis:
ut non declínet cor meum in verba malítiæ, ad excusándas excusatiónes in peccátis.
priestEvents.Action: Incenses cross and altar while reciting Dirigatur.

priestEvents.Trigger_Text: Accéndat in nobis Dóminus ignem sui amóris, et flammam ætérnæ caritátis. Amen.
priestEvents.Action: Returns the thurible while saying Accendat.

priestEvents.Trigger_Text: [CELEBRANT, CLERGY AND PEOPLE ARE INCENSED AS THE SUNG-MASS FORM REQUIRES]

priestEvents.Trigger_Text:
Ps 25, 6–12
Lavábo inter innocéntes manus meas: et circúmdabo altáre tuum, Dómine:
Ut áudiam vocem laudis, et enárrem univérsa mirabília tua.
Dómine, diléxi decórem domus tuæ et locum habitatiónis glóriæ tuæ.
Ne perdas cum ímpiis, Deus, ánimam meam, et cum viris sánguinum vitam meam:
In quorum mánibus iniquitátes sunt: déxtera eórum repléta est munéribus.
Ego autem in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum: rédime me et miserére mei.
Pes meus stetit in dirécto: in ecclésiis benedícam te, Dómine.
priestEvents.Action: At the Epistle side, washes the prescribed fingers while reciting Psalm 25.

priestEvents.Trigger_Text: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
priestEvents.Action: Bows his head at Gloria Patri.

priestEvents.Trigger_Text: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper: et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
priestEvents.Action: Raises his head and completes the psalm.

priestEvents.Trigger_Text: Súscipe, sancta Trinitas, hanc oblatiónem, quam tibi offérimus ob memóriam passiónis, resurrectiónis, et ascensiónis Iesu Christi, Dómini nostri: et in honórem beátæ Maríæ semper Vírginis, et beáti Ioannis Baptistæ, et sanctórum Apostolórum Petri et Pauli, et istórum et ómnium Sanctórum: ut illis profíciat ad honórem, nobis autem ad salútem: et illi pro nobis intercédere dignéntur in coelis, quorum memóriam ágimus in terris. Per eúndem Christum, Dóminum nostrum. Amen.
priestEvents.Action: At the centre, bows somewhat with hands joined on the altar while saying the prayer privately.

priestEvents.Trigger_Text: [KISSES THE ALTAR — PREPARES TO TURN TO THE PEOPLE]

priestEvents.Trigger_Text: Oráte, fratres:

priestEvents.Trigger_Text: In primis, quæ tibi offérimus pro Ecclésia tua sancta cathólica: quam pacificáre, custodíre, adunáre et régere dignéris toto orbe terrárum: una cum fámulo tuo Papa nostro N. et Antístite nostro et ómnibus orthodóxis, atque cathólicæ et apostólicae fídei cultóribus.

priestEvents.Trigger_Text: Communicántes, et memóriam venerántes, in primis gloriósæ semper Vírginis Maríæ, Genetrícis Dei et Dómini nostri
priestEvents.Posture: Standing at centre with hands extended

priestEvents.Posture: Standing at centre with hands extended
priestEvents.Action: Joins hands for the conclusion.

priestEvents.Trigger_Text: Hanc igitur oblatiónem servitutis nostræ, sed et cunctae famíliæ tuæ, quaesumus, Dómine, ut placátus accípias: diésque nostros in tua pace dispónas, atque ab ætérna damnatióne nos éripi, et in electórum tuórum iúbeas grege numerári.

priestEvents.Action: Extends both hands over the oblations.

priestEvents.Trigger_Text: tibi grátias agens,

priestEvents.Trigger_Text:
In princípio erat Verbum, et Verbum erat apud Deum, et Deus erat Verbum. Hoc erat in princípio apud Deum.
Ómnia per ipsum facta sunt: et sine ipso factum est nihil, quod factum est. In ipso vita erat, et vita erat lux hóminum:
et lux in ténebris lucet, et ténebræ eam non comprehendérunt.
priestEvents.Action: Reads Last Gospel

priestEvents.Trigger_Text:
Fuit homo missus a Deo, cui nomen erat Ioánnes. Hic venit in testimónium, ut testimónium perhibéret de lúmine,
ut omnes créderent per illum. Non erat ille lux, sed ut testimónium perhibéret de lúmine. Erat lux vera,
quæ illúminat omnem hóminem veniéntem in hunc mundum. In mundo erat, et mundus per ipsum factus est,
et mundus eum non cognóvit. In própria venit, et sui eum non recepérunt. Quotquot autem recepérunt eum,
dedit eis potestátem fílios Dei fíeri, his, qui credunt in nómine eius: qui non ex sanguínibus, neque ex voluntáte carnis,
neque ex voluntáte viri, sed ex Deo nati sunt.

concurrency.Rule_or_Reality: Introit is the public liturgical clock while the priest’s preparatory prayers are quiet.
concurrency.User_Guidance: Follow the Introit: sing, listen, or meditate on the public chant. Keep the posture shown. You do not need to keep pace with the priest’s quiet preparatory prayers.

concurrency.Rule_or_Reality: Stay with the sung Kyrie until its final invocation.
concurrency.User_Guidance: Follow the public Kyrie. Keep the posture shown; follow the sung invocations rather than the priest’s private pace.

concurrency.Rule_or_Reality: After the priest’s intonation, the choir carries the public Gloria; return to Priest at the final Amen.
concurrency.User_Guidance: Follow the sung Gloria and the gesture cues attached to its actual words. Change posture only when the active cue tells you to do so.
concurrency.Safe_Next_Cue: Collect after the public Gloria ends.

concurrency.Rule_or_Reality: The Collect is a public priestly prayer.
concurrency.User_Guidance: Follow the public Collect after Dominus vobiscum and Oremus. Stand and attend to the prayer.

concurrency.Rule_or_Reality: At the end of the Epistle, the interlection chants become the public clock.
concurrency.User_Guidance: Follow the Epistle / Lesson. Sit and listen to the reading.

concurrency.Rule_or_Reality: When the chant complex ends, the public Gospel becomes the next clock.
concurrency.User_Guidance: Follow the Schola: Gradual, then the resolved Alleluia / Tract / Sequence. Remain seated until the Gospel cue approaches.

concurrency.Rule_or_Reality: The public Gospel controls.
concurrency.User_Guidance: Follow the public Gospel. Stand; make the three small crosses at the public announcement, then listen attentively.
concurrency.Safe_Next_Cue: Sermon if present; otherwise Credo or Offertory.

concurrency.Rule_or_Reality: Follow the preacher; Mass resumes only when the liturgical action resumes.
concurrency.User_Guidance: Follow the preacher. Sit and listen.

concurrency.Rule_or_Reality: After the priest’s intonation, follow the public sung Creed; return after Amen.
concurrency.User_Guidance: Follow the sung Credo and its public-text gesture cues. Use the active posture cue, especially at the Incarnatus.
concurrency.Locator: LU62/DMS58; RG60 Incarnatus exception where applicable

concurrency.Rule_or_Reality: Follow the Offertory chant while sounding; when it ends, the altar action becomes the better landmark.
concurrency.User_Guidance: While the Offertory chant is sounding, follow the public chant. When it ends, the visible preparation of the altar becomes the main landmark. Remain in the posture shown; respond to incensation only when it actually reaches your section.

concurrency.Rule_or_Reality: Orate fratres is public; the Secret is quiet but the priest remains the useful clock.
concurrency.User_Guidance: Give priority to the public Orate fratres and response. During the silent Secret, remain recollected rather than trying to synchronize to the priest’s words. Keep the posture shown.
concurrency.Safe_Next_Cue: The public Per omnia / Preface dialogue.

concurrency.Rule_or_Reality: At the end of the Preface, the Sanctus begins.
concurrency.User_Guidance: Follow the public Preface dialogue and Preface. Stand and answer the dialogue.

concurrency.Rule_or_Reality: Follow Sanctus/Benedictus while sung; when the choir falls silent, the Canon may be followed on the priest track.
concurrency.User_Guidance: Follow the Schola’s Sanctus / Benedictus while it is actually being sung. Stand through the current chant; prepare to kneel as the Canon takes over.

concurrency.Rule_or_Reality: The Canon is secret; following the text is optional. Warning bell/elevations override both tracks.
concurrency.User_Guidance: The main cue is now sacred silence and interior participation. Kneel. Unite yourself with the Sacrifice; remain attentive for the warning bell and visible Consecration landmarks.
concurrency.Safe_Next_Cue: Warning bell → Consecration of the Sacred Host.

concurrency.Rule_or_Reality: The elevation is the decisive visual/sacramental landmark.
concurrency.User_Guidance: The Consecration and visible elevation of the Sacred Host have priority over everything else. Remain kneeling; bow reverently and look upon the Sacred Host when elevated.

concurrency.Rule_or_Reality: The elevation is the decisive visual/sacramental landmark.
concurrency.User_Guidance: The Consecration and visible elevation of the Chalice have priority. Remain kneeling and attend to the elevation.

concurrency.Rule_or_Reality: If Benedictus resumes, follow it; otherwise remain in sacred silence / priest Canon.
concurrency.User_Guidance: If the Benedictus resumes, follow that public chant; otherwise the main mode is sacred silence and interior participation. Keep the posture of your local/profile setting.

concurrency.Rule_or_Reality: Minor elevation and public Per omnia reset the common timeline.
concurrency.User_Guidance: Follow the visible minor elevation and then the public Per omnia. Use the public conclusion as the clean reset into the Communion rite.

concurrency.Rule_or_Reality: Pater noster is public.
concurrency.User_Guidance: Follow the public Pater noster and the Sed libera response. Stand and make the response when it is actually due.

concurrency.Rule_or_Reality: After Pax Domini the Agnus becomes the public sung clock.
concurrency.User_Guidance: During silent Libera nos, use the visible Fraction as the landmark; when Pax Domini is heard, the public cue takes priority. Stand until the next posture cue.

concurrency.Rule_or_Reality: After Agnus, private Communion preparation follows.
concurrency.User_Guidance: Follow the sung Agnus Dei. Make the ordinary breast strikes with the sung invocations; prepare to kneel for Communion preparation.

concurrency.Rule_or_Reality: Priest’s private prayers may be followed, but interior preparation is primary.
concurrency.User_Guidance: The main mode is recollection and interior preparation for Communion. Kneel and prepare yourself for Communion.

concurrency.Rule_or_Reality: Visible Communion of the priest is the landmark.
concurrency.User_Guidance: The visible Communion of the priest is now the main landmark. Remain kneeling and prepare for the public Communion invitation if the faithful will receive.
concurrency.Safe_Next_Cue: Ecce Agnus Dei, if the faithful receive.

concurrency.Rule_or_Reality: Once distribution begins, the Communion chant is useful while waiting.
concurrency.User_Guidance: The public Ecce Agnus Dei and the faithful’s Domine non sum dignus have priority. Remain kneeling and make the response/associated action when it is actually due.

concurrency.Rule_or_Reality: Your own Communion turn overrides both tracks; otherwise follow Communion chant/distribution.
concurrency.User_Guidance: Your personal Communion action has priority when your turn actually comes; otherwise follow the Communion chant and visible distribution. Approach, receive, and return according to your actual place in the Communion line.
concurrency.Locator: Ritus X; DMS58 Communion chant timing

concurrency.Rule_or_Reality: Stay with Communion chant while it sounds; switch when chant/distribution end and ablutions dominate.
concurrency.User_Guidance: If the Communion chant is still sounding, follow it; otherwise the priest’s visible return and ablutions are the main landmark. Use the local/profile posture shown and prepare to stand for the Postcommunion.

concurrency.Rule_or_Reality: Postcommunion is public.
concurrency.User_Guidance: Follow the public Postcommunion after Dominus vobiscum and Oremus. Stand and attend to the prayer.

concurrency.Rule_or_Reality: Dismissal is public; Schola/people give the response.
concurrency.User_Guidance: Follow the public dismissal and response. Stand and make the response.

concurrency.Rule_or_Reality: Quiet Placeat leads into the visible final blessing.
concurrency.User_Guidance: During the quiet Placeat, remain recollected. When the priest turns for the final blessing, that public visible action takes priority. Kneel for the blessing where appointed, then rise for the Last Gospel.

concurrency.Rule_or_Reality: Last Gospel is the public final text unless omitted by a special branch.
concurrency.User_Guidance: Follow the public Last Gospel. Stand; genuflect at Et Verbum caro factum est, then rise.

concurrency.Rule_or_Reality: Follow the public antiphon while the priest sprinkles; the final Amen hands directly to the Mass Introit.
concurrency.User_Guidance: Stand; sign yourself when actually sprinkled.

concurrency.Rule_or_Reality: The Improperia are a soundtrack to the queue, not the trigger for your action.
concurrency.User_Guidance: When your turn reaches the Cross, perform the prescribed personal reverence/veneration.

Lesson from the Epistle of blessed Paul the Apostle to the Ephesians.
Brethren: Be renewed in the spirit of your mind, and put on the new man, who according to God is created in justice and holiness of truth. Therefore, putting away falsehood, let each speak truth with his neighbour, for we are members one of another. Be angry, and sin not; let not the sun go down upon your anger. Give no place to the devil. He that stole, let him now steal no more, but rather let him labour, working with his hands at that which is good, that he may have wherewith to give to him that suffereth need.
℟. Thanks be to God.

fixture.Latin_Text:
In illo témpore: Loquebátur Iesus princípibus sacerdótum et pharisǽis in parábolis, dicens: Símile factum est regnum cœlórum hómini regi, qui fecit núptias fílio suo. Et misit servos suos vocáre invitátos ad núptias, et nolébant veníre. Iterum misit álios servos, dicens: Dícite invitátis: Ecce, prándium meum parávi, tauri mei et altília occísa sunt, et ómnia paráta: veníte ad núptias. Illi autem neglexérunt: et abiérunt, álius in villam suam, álius vero ad negotiatiónem suam: réliqui vero tenuérunt servos eius, et contuméliis afféctos occidérunt. Rex autem cum audísset, irátus est: et, missis exercítibus suis, pérdidit homicídas illos et civitátem illórum succéndit. Tunc ait servis suis: Núptiæ quidem parátæ sunt, sed, qui invitáti erant, non fuérunt digni. Ite ergo ad éxitus viárum et, quoscúmque invenéritis, vocáte ad núptias. Et egréssi servi eius in vias, congregavérunt omnes, quos invenérunt, malos et bonos: et implétæ sunt núptiæ discumbéntium. Intrávit autem rex, ut vidéret discumbéntes, et vidit ibi hóminem non vestítum veste nuptiáli. Et ait illi: Amíce, quómodo huc intrásti non habens vestem nuptiálem? At ille obmútuit. Tunc dixit rex minístris: Ligátis mánibus et pédibus eius, míttite eum in ténebras exterióres: ibi erit fletus et stridor déntium. Multi enim sunt vocáti, pauci vero elécti.
℟. Laus tibi, Christe.
Per evangélica dicta deleántur nostra delícta.
fixture.English_Text:
At that time Jesus spoke to the chief priests and Pharisees in parables, saying: The kingdom of heaven is like a king who made a marriage feast for his son. He sent his servants to call those invited to the wedding, but they would not come. Again he sent other servants, saying: Tell those who are invited: Behold, I have prepared my banquet; my oxen and fattened cattle are killed, and all things are ready; come to the wedding. But they paid no heed and went away, one to his farm and another to his business; the rest seized his servants, treated them shamefully, and killed them. When the king heard of it he was angry, and sent his armies, destroyed those murderers, and burned their city. Then he said to his servants: The wedding indeed is ready, but those who were invited were not worthy. Go therefore to the crossroads, and whomever you shall find, call to the wedding. Going out into the roads, the servants gathered all whom they found, bad and good alike, and the wedding was filled with guests. The king entered to see the guests and saw there a man not clothed in a wedding garment. He said to him: Friend, how didst thou enter here without a wedding garment? But he was speechless. Then the king said to the servants: Bind his hands and feet and cast him into the outer darkness; there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth. For many are called, but few are chosen.
℟. Praise be to Thee, O Christ.
By the words of the Gospel may our sins be blotted out.

fixture.Resolved_Title: Preface of the Most Holy Trinity
fixture.Latin_Text: Vere dignum et iustum est, æquum et salutáre, nos tibi semper et ubíque grátias ágere: Dómine sancte, Pater omnípotens, ætérne Deus: Qui cum unigénito Fílio tuo et Spíritu Sancto unus es Deus, unus es Dóminus: non in uníus singularitáte persónæ, sed in uníus Trinitáte substántiæ. Quod enim de tua glória, revelánte te, crédimus, hoc de Fílio tuo, hoc de Spíritu Sancto sine differéntia discretiónis sentímus. Ut in confessióne veræ sempiternǽque Deitátis, et in persónis propríetas, et in esséntia únitas, et in maiestáte adorétur æquálitas. Quam laudant Angeli atque Archángeli, Chérubim quoque ac Séraphim: qui non cessant clamáre cotídie, una voce dicéntes:
fixture.English_Text: It is truly meet and just, right and profitable unto salvation, that we should at all times and in all places give thanks unto Thee, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: Who with Thine only-begotten Son and the Holy Ghost art one God, one Lord; not in the singleness of one Person, but in the Trinity of one substance. For what, by Thy revelation, we believe of Thy glory, the same we believe of Thy Son and of the Holy Ghost, without difference or distinction; so that, in confessing the true and everlasting Godhead, distinction in Persons, unity in essence, and equality in majesty may be adored. Which the Angels and Archangels, the Cherubim also and Seraphim praise, who cease not daily to cry out with one voice, saying:
